original_request: Combine Pitch A and B: Build Python intelligence-layer daemon that absorbs bash peer-review engine logic, adds intent parsing, universal routing, prompt compilation per destination, SQLite effectiveness tracking. Wire into Right Hand input loop for universal coverage. Integrate with peer-review-config.json, dispatch system, Discord components v2, session management.

enrichment.enriched_description: Build `intelligence/` Python package containing a long-running daemon that replaces the bash peer-review pipeline (peer-review-score.sh + peer-review-engine.sh) with a unified Python intelligence layer. The daemon exposes a socket/stdin loop that Right Hand feeds all incoming requests into. It must: (1) parse intent from raw text to extract domain, complexity score, detected agent, and structured subtasks; (2) route universally using peer-review-config.json domain_map and complexity thresholds; (3) compile destination-specific prompts per agent with vault refs injected; (4) track pipeline effectiveness in SQLite (replacing the JSONL log); (5) emit Discord components v2 formatted stage-by-stage messages; (6) integrate session-dispatch-protocol for session matching before spawning; (7) wire into dispatch-engine.sh as the pre-spawn intelligence phase. Entry point: `intelligence/daemon.py`. Config consumed from peer-review-config.json at ~/workspace. SQLite db at ~/dispatch/peer-review/effectiveness.db.
subtasks: Read ~/bin/peer-review-score.sh and ~/bin/peer-review-engine.sh to extract all scoring heuristics, enrichment logic, and consultant deliberation prompts before writing any Python

Design SQLite schema: tables for pipeline_runs (task_id, domain, complexity, pipeline_path, agent, timestamps), stage_events (task_id, stage, status, duration_ms, payload), effectiveness_scores (task_id, completion, quality, enrichment_value, efficiency, notes)

Implement intelligence/intent_parser.py: IntentParser class with parse(raw_text) -> IntentResult(domain, complexity_score, detected_agent, keywords, subtasks_hint); port keyword/heuristic scoring from bash peer-review-score.sh

Implement intelligence/router.py: UniversalRouter class that loads peer-review-config.json, selects pipeline_path (fast_track/light_review/full_review) based on complexity_score, selects consultants via domain_map, returns RouteDecision(pipeline, consultants, vault_refs, timeouts)

Implement intelligence/prompt_compiler.py: PromptCompiler class with compile(task, route_decision, stage) -> str; per-destination prompt templates for enrich/deliberate/refine stages with vault refs injected; consultant-specific prompt variants (coder, security, researcher, etc.)

Implement intelligence/tracker.py: EffectivenessTracker class backed by SQLite using WAL mode; methods: start_run, record_stage, complete_run, score_run, query_stats; replaces ~/dispatch/peer-review/effectiveness-log.jsonl

Implement intelligence/discord_emitter.py: DiscordEmitter class that builds components v2 containers per stage (INTAKE, ENRICH, DELIBERATE, REFINE, EXECUTE, POST_REVIEW) with correct agent color/emoji from discord-output-format.md; includes identity bar and routing line on every message
Implement intelligence/session_matcher.py: thin wrapper around session-manager.sh dispatch CLI call; returns SessionMatch(recommendation, session_id, score) for use in REFINE stage before agent spawn

Implement intelligence/daemon.py: IntelligenceDaemon main class with run_pipeline(raw_input, source_channel) orchestrating all 6 stages; input loop via stdin/named pipe watching ~/dispatch/queue/; health_check() method; graceful shutdown handler
Wire daemon into dispatch-engine.sh: daemon pre-processes task before _invoke_claude(); update AGENTS.md/peer-review-protocol.md to document Python daemon as replacement for bash scripts

Write tests in intelligence/tests/: unit tests for IntentParser (domain classification accuracy), Router (correct consultant selection per domain), PromptCompiler (vault refs present in output); integration test for full pipeline with mock Discord calls
enrichment.context_notes: peer-review-config.json is at ~/workspace with guild_id 1482230800916287710, 4 Discord channels (intake/deliberation/refined/post_review), complexity thresholds (fast_track<=2, light_review<=5, full_review>=6), domain_map with 9 domains. dispatch-engine.sh already has checkpoint phases (started->invoking->tool-call->summarizing->completed|failed) and a stubbed _invoke_claude() that needs the intelligence layer wired in before it. session-dispatch-protocol.md defines the session-manager.sh CLI that the daemon must call pre-spawn. discord-output-format.md defines components v2 format with 3-block containers, agent colors (#57A773 for Coder), and identity bar format. Effectiveness log currently JSONL at ~/dispatch/peer-review/effectiveness-log.jsonl — SQLite replaces this. bash scripts referenced in peer-review-protocol.md live at ~/bin/peer-review-engine.sh and ~/bin/peer-review-score.sh and MUST be read first before porting logic.
enrichment.success_criteria: 1) `python intelligence/daemon.py --health` exits 0 and prints all subsystems OK; 2) IntentParser correctly classifies domain for 8/9 domain types in test suite; 3) Full pipeline end-to-end test: input text flows through all 6 stages, Discord messages formatted correctly with identity bars, SQLite has records for the run; 4) session-manager.sh dispatch is called before agent spawn and result affects --resume vs new session decision; 5) peer-review-config.json domain_map drives consultant and vault_ref selection; 6) existing dispatch-engine.sh cmd_run still works with daemon as pre-processor
risk_factors: ~/bin/peer-review-score.sh and ~/bin/peer-review-engine.sh may not exist yet — daemon must degrade gracefully and not hard-depend on them at import time
SQLite WAL mode required to prevent lock contention when dispatch-engine.sh and daemon write concurrently
Intent parsing false positives (e.g. 'code review' classified as 'code' not 'prompt') will route to wrong consultant pool — needs confidence threshold with fallback to 'general'
Discord components v2 API requires specific JSON structure — test against actual channel before wiring into hot path
session-manager.sh is a shell script with its own registry at ~/dispatch/session-registry.json — subprocess call must handle non-zero exit codes and timeouts gracefully
Named pipe / stdin input loop must handle Right Hand sending multiple concurrent tasks without blocking — use asyncio or threading
verification_steps: python -m pytest intelligence/tests/ -v --tb=short — all tests pass
python intelligence/daemon.py --health — prints subsystem status for parser/router/compiler/tracker/discord/session
echo 'Build a Python scraper for reddit API' | python intelligence/daemon.py --dry-run — prints full pipeline JSON with domain=code, consultants=[coder, prompt-engineer], vault_refs populated
sqlite3 ~/dispatch/peer-review/effectiveness.db 'SELECT count(*) FROM pipeline_runs' — returns > 0 after dry-run test
Verify Discord components v2 structure: check emitted JSON has container.accentColor, blocks[0..2] with text types, blocks[1] contains agent name and mode
bash dispatch-engine.sh run test-001 coder /tmp/test-msg.txt — confirm intelligence layer fires pre-invocation and checkpoint advances through all phases

deliberation.coder:
IMPROVEMENTS

1. IntentParser must have a `confidence: float` field in IntentResult and a `CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.6` constant — if below threshold, domain falls back to `"general"` before routing. The risk factor names this but the subtask doesn't implement it.

2. Daemon input loop must use `asyncio` with a named pipe (`~/dispatch/queue/intelligence.pipe`) rather than stdin — Right Hand can't reliably own stdin if dispatch-engine.sh also needs to feed tasks. Create the pipe in daemon startup, not assumed present.

3. SQLite schema is missing `source_channel TEXT` and `raw_input_hash TEXT` (SHA-256) on `pipeline_runs` — needed for deduplication when dispatch-engine.sh retries and for correlating Discord messages back to DB records.

4. PromptCompiler vault_refs injection must read actual file snippets (first 500 chars), not just inject paths as strings — the plan says "vault refs injected" but if it's just filenames the prompts are useless.

5. Add `intelligence/config.py` as a dataclass-backed config loader that validates peer-review-config.json schema on load (pydantic or dataclasses + manual checks) — runtime schema violations in the middle of a pipeline run are far worse than a startup failure.

MISSING ELEMENTS

6. No `intelligence/__init__.py` with `__version__` and public API surface defined — the daemon import path will break when dispatch-engine.sh calls `python -m intelligence.daemon` vs `python intelligence/daemon.py` depending on CWD. Pin the entry point explicitly.

7. No database migration strategy — first run creates schema, but if schema changes between versions, `effectiveness.db` will have wrong columns. Add a `SCHEMA_VERSION` table and `migrate()` function called at startup.

8. No timeout enforcement inside the pipeline — if session-manager.sh hangs, the whole daemon blocks. Every subprocess call (session_matcher, discord emit) needs `asyncio.wait_for` with the timeout values from peer-review-config.json.

CONSTRAINTS

9. WAL mode must be set via `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` AND `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL` in the same connection setup — WAL alone without synchronous=NORMAL gives no real concurrency improvement. Set both in `tracker.py` connection initialization.

10. Discord components v2 `accentColor` must be an integer (RGB as decimal), not a hex string — `#57A773` must be stored/emitted as `5742451`. Wrong type silently breaks Discord rendering with no error.

RISKS

11. peer-review-score.sh and peer-review-engine.sh may use bash arrays and process substitution that have no direct Python equivalent — the subtask says "port keyword/heuristic scoring" but doesn't account for this. Read both scripts before writing IntentParser, specifically looking for `mapfile`, `declare -A`, and pipeline chains that represent multi-step scoring.

12. Named pipe blocks on open until both reader and writer connect — if daemon starts before dispatch-engine.sh writes, `open(pipe, 'r')` hangs forever. Use `os.open(pipe, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NONBLOCK)` then wrap in `asyncio.StreamReader`.

VERDICT: APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES

Points 2 (asyncio named pipe), 5 (config validation at startup), 8 (subprocess timeouts), 10 (Discord integer color), and 12 (non-blocking pipe open) are blocking — ship any of these wrong and the daemon either deadlocks or silently corrupts output. The rest are quality improvements that should be incorporated before first test run.
deliberation.prompt-engineer:
**PROMPT ENGINEERING SPECIALIST REVIEW**

**Improvements**

1. **PromptCompiler subtask is critically underspecified.** "Per-destination prompt templates" needs a defined structure: identity block → cognitive_thought mandate → task description → vault refs section → output schema → failure protocol. Without this skeleton, the compiler will produce inconsistent prompts across stages.

2. **Mandate `<cognitive_thought>` blocks in Coder/Security compiled prompts.** APEX-Hybrid-Analysis.md in your own vault explicitly validates this pattern. Add it as a required pre-generation block in PromptCompiler for those two agent types: Intent Decoupling → Context Analysis → Strategy → Risk Assessment.

3. **Define what actually differs between consultant variants.** The plan says "consultant-specific prompt variants (coder, security, researcher)" but doesn't specify the delta. Is it only the identity block? Tool permissions? Output format? Specify exactly what PromptCompiler.compile() overrides per agent type — otherwise it becomes a giant if/else with no principle.

4. **Specify deliberation stage output schema.** The deliberate stage prompt must instruct consultants to emit structured output (JSON or tagged sections). If it's free-form prose, EffectivenessTracker can't reliably parse stage_events or score quality. Add a required output schema to the deliberate prompt template spec.

**Missing Elements**

5. **No few-shot examples in compiled prompts.** Production agents (EliFuzz corpus) use worked examples heavily. PromptCompiler should include at minimum one canonical example per stage type (enrich/deliberate/refine). Add this to the subtask 5 specification.

6. **No token budget / vault ref truncation strategy.** Three vault refs × ~2KB each = ~6KB per compile call before the actual task. At high complexity runs, this risks context overflow. The plan needs a defined priority/truncation strategy: which sections of vault refs to include, max chars per ref, and what to drop first.

7. **No prompt versioning tied to effectiveness tracking.** SQLite schema tracks run outcomes but not which prompt template version produced them. Add a `prompt_template_version` column to `pipeline_runs` and a `prompt_templates` table. This makes the effectiveness scores actually usable for improving prompts over time.

8. **Confidence-uncertain domain handling is missing from PromptCompiler.** risk_factors mentions confidence threshold fallback to 'general' but PromptCompiler subtask doesn't specify what a 'general' domain compiled prompt looks like or which consultants it routes to. Add a fallback template spec.

**Constraints**

9. **Behavioral rules in compiled prompts must be priority-ordered.** Per System Prompt Patterns reference: NEVER → ALWAYS → PREFER → WHEN. PromptCompiler must enforce this ordering in every emitted prompt, not rely on the template author to get it right.

10. **Vault ref injection must be labeled, not verbatim-appended.** Each injected ref needs a relevance label (`## Reference: [title] (relevance: [why])`). Raw append without context label causes instruction bleed — the agent won't know why it was given the ref or how much weight to give it.

**Risks**

11. **Prompt drift on vault ref content changes.** If a referenced vault file changes, compiled prompts silently change behavior with no signal in the effectiveness log. Add a vault_ref content hash to `pipeline_runs` so regressions from vault edits are detectable.

12. **Multi-consultant deliberation produces conflicting outputs with no resolution protocol.** If domain_map routes to [coder, security] and they disagree, the refine stage has no instruction on how to adjudicate. The deliberate stage prompt template must specify either: consensus required, primary consultant has final say, or escalation to Right Hand.

**Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES**

Core architecture is solid. Block on subtask 5 (PromptCompiler) until the template skeleton, output schema, few-shot examples, and token budget strategy are specified. Everything else can proceed in parallel. The SQLite schema (subtask 2) should also add `prompt_template_version` before implementation begins.
